title: How do deceptive slipper-type orchid flowers attract pollinators?
fixture_notice: TEST FIXTURE. The structure models a real kind of dispute (two competing deception mechanisms). Evidence and provenance entries are synthetic placeholders with citation_status 'unverified-fixture'. They are not literature claims and must not be published or cited.

claims.statement: Pollinators are drawn to the flowers by deception rather than by a reward, but the evidence does not yet establish which deceptive signal is responsible.

mechanisms.label: Food deception: the flower imitates a nectar or pollen source
mechanisms.distinguishing_observation: visitors probe the lip and leave quickly without feeding behaviour

mechanisms.label: Oviposition-site mimicry: the flower imitates a place to lay eggs
mechanisms.distinguishing_observation: visiting flies deposit eggs or show egg-laying posture on the flower

uncertainty.statement: The available observations are compatible with both mechanisms and cannot currently separate them.
uncertainty.reason: Visitor behaviour was recorded in too few visits to distinguish probing for food from searching for an egg-laying site.
